title: tunnelmind:data_model:v1 — structured query artifact
description: profile_artifacts/queries/{query_sha256}.json: the structured query an assessment or golden question names by query_sha256 — metric, dimensions, filters, time range. No field admits free text (ATAP §7.6): metric and dimensions are field_refs, a filter value is only a number, a boolean or an opaque token (no `@`, no whitespace, containing no IPv4/IPv6/CIDR shape or `did:`; see $defs.scalar), and every object sets additionalProperties:false. A question in natural language, an email, an IP address, a did: key id or a name typed with spaces has nowhere to go; a name written as one token (`jane.doe`) is not detected by shape. time_range.from must be strictly earlier than to; the schema cannot compare dates, so the profile-aware verifier checks it (profile §9).

field_ref.description: Same pattern as witness-events.schema.json field_ref: dotted lower-case identifiers only.

scalar.description: A filter value: a number, a boolean, or an opaque token (an enum member such as `failure` or `eap-tls` is an opaque token). Same token pattern as witness-events.schema.json opaque_id: no `@`, no whitespace; and the unanchored `not` rejects a value that contains, anywhere, a dotted quad (`[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}`), a `::`, a hex group followed by two or more `:`-separated hex groups (`[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,4}(:[0-9A-Fa-f]{0,4}){2,}`), a trailing CIDR suffix (`/[0-9]{1,3}` at the end) or `did:` in any case. It is a heuristic against address- and key-shaped values, not a proof that a token names no person or host. An opaque token is not checked for being a person's name: `jane.doe` has the same shape as an enum member and passes.
